summary: The S&P 500 lost ~8.6% in the week to Nov 20 — a seven-session losing streak capped by a -3.7% Friday to 6,910.39, its first close under 7,000 since April — then ripped +4.73% to 7,237.17 on Nov 23 after NVIDIA's board reinstated Jensen Huang (NVDA +31%, Nasdaq +6.5%). Even after the relief rally the index is still ~1.4% below its 200-day (~7,340) and ~7% off the 7,819 high, VIX is 27 (down from 35.9 but still inverted vs VIX3M on Friday), only ~43% of stocks sit above their 50-day, and HY spreads widened to ~3.52%. A Dec 9 +25bp hike is ~91% priced; October PCE (Nov 25, core consensus 3.2% y/y) is the last inflation print before the Fed. Don't chase a one-day squeeze — wait for the S&P to reclaim its 200-day and VIX to fall back under ~22.
